validity.recommendation: Correct StartYear1 from 2022 to 2021 (in-service Dec 1, 2021 per FERC EA schedule, EIA's 2022-01-14 Completed record, and National Fuel's FY2022 annual report to shareholders). Also update Diameter to reflect the project's mixed pipe sizes.
validity.researcher_notes: The row (FM 100 Project, National Fuel Gas Supply Corp, docket CP19-491-000, pre-filing PF17-10-000) is REAL and correctly classified as an operating interstate gas transmission project. Existence/classification: confirmed via FERC's own EA (CP19-491-EA.pdf), the Federal Register application/EA-availability notices, PA DEP's Pipeline Portal FM100 page, National Fuel's FY2022 annual report to shareholders (SEC EDGAR), NGI trade press, and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (project_key 'fm 100 project|national fuel gas supply corp', tracked since the 2019-05 release). No duplicate: this is distinct from P6878 (NFG Supply Main Line, the parent trunk) -- FM100 built new lateral/loop/extension pipe (Line YM58, YM224 Loop, KL Extension) plus two new compressor stations tying into that mainline; it did not restate the mainline's own length/capacity. SPEC finding: the FERC EA's facility list gives exactly 29.5 mi (20-in, Line YM58) + 1.4 mi (24-in loop, Line YM224) + 0.4 mi (12-in extension, Line KL) = 31.3 mi total -- this matches the sheet's LengthKnown=31.3 mi EXACTLY and confirms Capacity=330 MMcf/d (=330,000 Dth/d per FERC/NGI) and the sheet's single Diameter=20in as the PREDOMINANT (not sole) pipe size; the loop and extension segments are 24-in and 12-in respectively, so the roster's other multi-diameter convention ('20, 24, 12') would be more complete, but 20in is not wrong as the majority figure -- flagging as a caveat, not an error, and giving the candidate multi-value string. SPEC concern (material): the sheet's StartYear1=2022 disagrees with FOUR converging independent sources that all place the in-service date at December 1, 2021: (1) FERC's EA (CP19-491-EA.pdf, section A.7 Construction Schedule): 'National Fuel proposes to begin pipeline and aboveground facility construction in early 2021 to place the FM100 Project into service by December 2021'; (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook first shows the project 'Completed' with completed_date 2021-12-01 in its 2022-01 release (last_updated_date 2022-01-14); (3) National Fuel's FY2022 Annual Report to Shareholders (SEC EDGAR, d425145dars.pdf) states the company 'completed construction of the FM100 project' -- 'the largest in the Company's history, was completed on time and substantially under budget' at a final cost of '$230 million'; (4) NGI trade press corroborates the FERC-authorized Dec-2021 target. The route geojson's own LastUpdated (2022-07-22) and StartYear1 (2022) appear to have picked up the FY2022 annual-report PUBLICATION year rather than the calendar in-service date -- an easy mix-up given National Fuel's fiscal year runs Oct-Sep, so 'completed in fiscal 2022' spans a project that actually entered service in December 2021 (calendar). Recommend StartYear1=2021 with StartMonth1=12.

validity.recommendation: Clear Delayed/DelayType -- the project was completed on schedule, not delayed.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's uncited Delayed=yes / DelayType=inferred is contradicted by the record: FERC's EA (Feb 2020) scheduled construction for early 2021 and in-service by December 2021, and National Fuel's own FY2022 annual report to shareholders states the FM100 project 'was completed on time and substantially under budget.' EIA's workbook shows a clean Applied -> Construction (2021-07) -> Completed (2022-01, completed_date 2021-12-01) progression with no gap or stall recorded. Nothing found supports an actual delay; this reads as a stale/incorrect inferred flag rather than a sourced finding. No ref exists to REVERIFY the current 'yes', so the fill below is UNRESOLVED rather than a fabricated confirmation -- the correction belongs here in validity, per the ADDENDUM's clearing recipe.
